questions.text: What is the most important starting point for developing personal Time Intelligence?
options: Creating a strict timetable for every hour
Understanding how beliefs, choices and constraints shape time use
Downloading a productivity application
Increasing the number of tasks completed daily

questions.text: Someone believes they must respond immediately to every request, even when it disrupts important activities. Which factor is most directly influencing their time use?
options: Their available weekly hours
Their personal belief about availability
Their technical productivity skills
Their physical working environment

questions.text: Which example best illustrates a realistic constraint rather than an avoidable time habit?
options: Repeatedly checking notifications without a purpose
Attending a scheduled medical appointment for a dependent
Opening social media whenever a task feels difficult
Revisiting the same email without taking action

questions.text: How many hours are available in a standard seven-day week?
options: 144 hours
160 hours
168 hours
176 hours

questions.text: A person spends 56 hours sleeping, 45 working and commuting, 30 on care and household duties, and 17 on personal care. How many hours remain?
options: 15 hours
20 hours
25 hours
30 hours

questions.text: Why is it misleading to assume that all hours remaining after fixed commitments are freely usable?
options: Because every remaining hour must be assigned to work
Because available time may still contain recovery, unpredictable needs and other responsibilities
Because discretionary time cannot be measured
Because personal planning is only useful during working hours

questions.text: Which statement most accurately distinguishes being busy, productive and effective?
options: Busy means producing outcomes, while effective means working longer
Productive means completing the largest number of tasks regardless of value
Busy refers to activity, productive to useful outputs, and effective to meaningful outcomes
All three terms measure the same aspect of time utilisation

questions.text: A learner spends two hours reading and can now explain a difficult concept accurately. Which is the clearest example of an outcome?
options: Opening the textbook
Spending two hours reading
Completing the assigned chapters
Demonstrating improved understanding

questions.text: A project manager attends six meetings, sends 40 emails and updates a tracker, but a critical decision remains unresolved. What is the strongest conclusion?
options: The manager has been effective because many activities were completed
The manager was active and produced an output, but the intended outcome remains incomplete
The manager was unproductive because no work was performed
The manager should eliminate all meetings immediately

questions.text: Which example is most clearly a recurring time leak?
options: Taking a necessary rest break
Providing essential care to a family member
Repeatedly searching for misplaced files because no consistent storage method exists
Attending a required appointment

questions.text: An avoidable interruption takes 12 minutes and happens three times daily over five working days. What is the weekly time cost?
options: 60 minutes
120 minutes
180 minutes
240 minutes

questions.text: What is the main purpose of using a Five Whys investigation on recurring time losses?
options: To identify who should be blamed for delays
To establish a deeper cause behind the recurring problem
To calculate the total number of hours in a week
To ensure that every task is completed more quickly

questions.text: Which sequence best represents the habit loop described in Week 1?
options: Outcome → deadline → schedule → reward
Cue → response → short-term effect → long-term pattern
Priority → delegation → performance → promotion
Planning → measurement → reporting → evaluation

questions.text: A notification arrives while someone is completing an important personal task. What is the best application of the 30-second decision filter?
options: Open the notification automatically
Ignore every notification without considering its importance
Check whether the interruption is essential or genuinely time-sensitive before deciding
Abandon the current task and reorganise the entire day

questions.text: Which approach is most appropriate when trying to replace an unhelpful daily habit?
options: Remove the habit without identifying what triggers it
Set an unrealistic target to create pressure
Identify the trigger, choose a useful replacement and monitor the change
Depend entirely on motivation to avoid the behaviour

questions.text: Why should personal roles and responsibilities be considered when planning time?
options: Because professional tasks should always take priority
Because realistic plans must account for care, health, relationships, work and other commitments
Because every role should receive exactly the same number of hours
Because responsibilities can always be removed through better planning

questions.text: A person faces a client deadline, a fixed school collection time and an optional social event. Which response best reflects Time Intelligence?
options: Accept every commitment and compensate by removing sleep
Protect essential responsibilities, assess consequences and negotiate or reschedule flexible commitments
Cancel school collection because work is always more important
Choose whichever activity feels easiest

questions.text: Which statement is the most effective way to communicate limited capacity?
options: I will try to do everything, although I cannot promise any result
Your request is unreasonable, so I will not consider it
I can complete the first task by Friday; the second would need Monday
I am too busy to discuss priorities

questions.text: The Week 1 Time Intelligence Diagnostic contains 24 statements across six dimensions, scored from 1 to 5. What is the possible total score range?
What is the most appropriate action after completing the Week 1 diagnostic?
options: Treat the score as a permanent measure of personal ability
Compare scores competitively with other participants
Identify patterns, choose one realistic improvement and review progress
Immediately attempt to change every aspect of time use

questions.text: Amara says improving her health is a major personal priority, but she repeatedly schedules optional activities during her planned exercise time. What should she do first?
options: Stop accepting all invitations indefinitely
Review whether her calendar choices reflect her stated values
Increase exercise intensity to compensate for missed sessions
Wait until she has a less demanding month

questions.text: Daniel has four goals: maintaining his health, supporting his children, developing a professional qualification and attending optional networking events. Which is the strongest basis for deciding how to allocate his limited time?
options: Choose whichever activity has the earliest invitation
Give equal time to all four goals regardless of circumstances
Consider personal values, consequences, deadlines and available capacity
Prioritise the goal that other people praise most

questions.text: A person has only one free hour this evening. They can either complete a course assignment due tomorrow or reorganise a cupboard that is already functional. What is the best choice?
options: Complete the assignment because it has a meaningful deadline and consequence
Reorganise the cupboard because it is easier to finish
Spend half an hour planning each task without starting either
Postpone both until the weekend

questions.text: Which task belongs in the ‘important but not urgent’ quadrant of the Eisenhower Matrix?
options: Responding to a time-critical safety concern
Completing a long-term savings plan before any immediate deadline
Responding to an unsolicited promotional message
Fixing an essential payment error due today

questions.text: A professional has a certification examination in six weeks. They repeatedly delay studying because no assignment is due this week. What is the main prioritisation mistake?
options: Confusing low urgency with low importance
Treating the examination as an emergency
Delegating too much preparation
Overestimating the value of daily breaks

questions.text: A participant has a medical appointment, a nonessential social invitation and a personal project milestone on the same afternoon. What is the most appropriate first step?
options: Cancel the medical appointment automatically
Accept all three and rely on multitasking
Assess which commitments are fixed, flexible and consequential
Choose the invitation received most recently

questions.text: Rita spends her mornings answering low-priority messages, leaving no time for a meaningful personal learning goal. Which change is most useful?
options: Check messages more frequently to clear them faster
Reserve a realistic learning period before routine message checking
Stop responding to all messages permanently
Extend every day by working late into the night

questions.text: A friend asks you to help organise an event during the only evening you have reserved for an important family commitment. What is the most constructive response?
options: Agree immediately to avoid disappointing your friend
Decline without any explanation or alternative
Explain your existing commitment and offer another realistic form of support if possible
Cancel the family commitment because helping others is always more important

questions.text: You are considering an optional weekend course that costs £200 and requires 12 hours. What is its opportunity cost?
options: Only the £200 course fee
Only the 12 hours spent attending
The value of the best alternative use of the money and time
The number of people who do not attend the course

questions.text: A participant accepts a new volunteer role despite already struggling with work, care responsibilities and recovery time. What is the most likely prioritisation risk?
options: The new role automatically becomes the highest priority
Adding a commitment without considering what it displaces may undermine existing priorities
Volunteering can never support personal values
Personal responsibilities should always be delegated

questions.text: A learner must choose between two valuable activities. One supports a long-term qualification; the other supports a short-term personal goal. Neither has an immediate deadline. What is the best decision method?
options: Always choose the shorter activity
Compare alignment with values, expected impact and realistic timing
Always choose the more expensive activity
Avoid making a decision until one becomes urgent

questions.text: A participant repeatedly says yes to requests because they fear appearing unhelpful. Which underlying issue should they examine?
options: Whether every request is objectively urgent
Whether approval-seeking is overriding their personal priorities and boundaries
Whether they should remove every personal commitment
Whether other people have more free time

questions.text: Which statement best demonstrates an effective personal boundary?
options: I will do everything you ask, but I may be exhausted
I cannot review this today; I can give it proper attention on Thursday
Your priorities are not important to me
I will respond whenever you remind me repeatedly

questions.text: Someone has committed to three optional evening activities but needs more time for rest and an important personal goal. Which strategy is most appropriate?
options: Reduce or decline one lower-value activity after reviewing the commitments
Keep every activity and reduce sleep
Assume the problem will disappear without making changes
Replace the personal goal with more social activities

questions.text: A person spends 40 minutes each day reviewing promotional emails they rarely use. Which action best fits the ‘eliminate’ decision?
options: Move the activity to a different time of day
Ask someone else to review every message
Unsubscribe from unnecessary promotional lists
Extend the activity to one hour

questions.text: A participant has a task that matters but does not require their personal involvement. Another capable person has agreed to handle it. Which decision is most suitable?
options: Eliminate the task regardless of its importance
Delegate the task with a clear expected result and deadline
Defer the task indefinitely
Continue doing the task personally to retain control

questions.text: A planned home improvement is useful but not time-sensitive, and the person is currently managing an unusually demanding month. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Treat it as an emergency
Defer it to a specific later review date
Remove essential rest to complete it immediately
Ignore the task permanently

questions.text: A person has to choose between an urgent request from someone else and a previously scheduled important personal commitment. What should they assess before changing plans?
options: Whether the requester sounds confident
The actual urgency, consequences and available alternatives
Whether the request arrived by phone or email
Whether the personal commitment is enjoyable

questions.text: Which approach best describes a useful personal priority hierarchy?
options: A permanent ranking that can never change
A list based entirely on what other people expect
An ordered guide reflecting values, essential responsibilities and current circumstances
A timetable that allocates identical hours to every role

questions.text: At the end of Week 2, which result would best demonstrate improved Priority Intelligence?
options: Having a calendar filled with activities
Being able to justify choices, protect meaningful commitments and adjust lower-value demands
Completing every request received from other people
Avoiding all unplanned situations
